Clay just raised a $115M Series D at a $7.1B valuation.

More than 17,000 teams build on Clay, including Anthropic, SpaceXAI, Google, OpenAI, Stripe, Visa, UPS — and 80% of the Forbes AI50.

The New York Times just broke the news, but the story goes far beyond the raise. AI is unleashing the biggest wave of company creation in history. Clay’s goal is to be the engine they use to grow.

We started as the company with the best data about other companies. Then we built the infrastructure to run campaigns across email, ads, and landing pages. 

Now we’re building agents that learn from every campaign, predict the next best action, and get better each time they run.

In 2023, we introduced GTME as a new role for people creating revenue systems with data, automation, and AI. Two years later, thousands of GTMEs are growing the world's best companies. They are gathering in nearly 100 Clay Clubs around the world, from Bangalore to Boston and Lahore to Lisbon.

A gracious thank you goes out to our customers, community, partners, team, and every GTM engineer shaping this with us.

OpenAI published a piece on how AI-native companies turn workflows into operating capability, and Clay shows up through something Solange Levy built for her own agentic-sales motion 👇

She pulled deal context from CRM, email, presentations, internal Slack channels, and champion updates into a persistent workspace with a subagent for every account.

Every morning, those agents help her surface the big priority moves that push deals forward:

> answer the open customer question
> find the missing person in the buying committee
> re-engage the quiet account
> check the source before acting

“The result is a shared evidence-based workspace for each account that helps me maintain momentum across every deal without reconstructing the story or the context over time," Solange says.

Clay's GTME MVP Sabrina Glaser went from "allergic to outbound" to closing $1M+ in outbound sales pipeline last quarter. Her flow is worth copying. 

This is LAST CALLLLLLLLLLL for How Clay Uses Clay: Cold Outbound to Enterprise Accounts: clay.link/5lUvXb3

Good reps already have the judgment about who to target, which signals matter, and what a real email should sound like.

Sabrina's problem was the slog before she could use that judgment (Salesforce for account history, Gong for past calls, social profiles for people, and Crunchbase/news/job posts/earnings calls for timing). All of it devoured her calendar.

So she built a 4-agent workflow that starts with one company domain:

1. pulls first-party account history
2. finds fresh third-party signals
3. maps 3-8 people in the buying center
4. drafts three sequences in her voice

The flow went internally-viral. Ashley Artrip saw the team-wide version, and Luca Prando helped turn it into a callable Clay CLI workflow with deliverability, dedupe, CRM mapping, and data governance wired in.

Now reps can run it from ChatGPT or Claude, review the work, and move.

We're walking through it live tomorrow. 

Be there or be square. 

((no seriously. she literally brought in more that $1 million. you're losing money by not attending 👀))

LANDED: We overhauled Clay Sequencer to bring your whole outbound motion into one place. Here's the 5 things we added:

1️⃣ 𝗔𝗹𝘄𝗮𝘆𝘀-𝗼𝗻 𝗹𝗲𝗮𝗱 𝘀𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗶𝗻𝗴: Find the fresh leads from your CRM, signal data, or Clay’s people database, then build dynamic lead and exclusion lists around them.

2️⃣ 𝗦𝗲𝗹𝗳-𝗾𝘂𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗳𝘆𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗹𝗲𝗮𝗱𝘀: Refresh your GTM data continuously, so accounts enter campaigns when they fit and leave when they don’t.

3️⃣ 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗲𝘅𝘁-𝗱𝗿𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗻 𝗰𝗼𝗽𝘆: Templates with AI snippets let you decide what gets personalized, using context from Clay’s 200+ data providers.

4️⃣ 𝗖𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗹𝗶𝘇𝗲𝗱 𝘀𝗲𝗻𝗱 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗱𝗲𝗹𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁: Buy inboxes and domains without leaving Clay, with warmup built in.

5️⃣ 𝗥𝗲𝗽𝗹𝗶𝗲𝘀 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱𝘆 𝗯𝗲𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗽𝘀 𝗼𝗽𝗲𝗻 𝗦𝗹𝗮𝗰𝗸: Auto-draft and share responses so your team can approve before sending.

Take this to your next meeting: the right pitch at the wrong time is the wrong pitch. Your context should be fresh, accurate, folded in from the start, and perfectly timed.
